content.text:
Markers can't be reached by Tab because they're drawn as SVG `CircleMarker` shapes, and Leaflet only makes `L.Marker` icons focusable. Even with that fixed, the order would be wrong on desktop: the map comes before the list panel in the page, so Tab reaches the map before the list. I read the code only; nothing was edited or run. Installed versions are leaflet 1.9.4 and react-leaflet 5.0.0.

## (a) Root causes

**1. The markers have no tab stop.** `ParkMap` draws each park as a `CircleMarker`:

```66:76:src/components/map/ParkMap.tsx
        {mappable.map(({ park, position }) => (
          <CircleMarker
            key={park.id ?? `${position[0]},${position[1]}`}
            center={position}
            radius={9}
            pathOptions={MARKER_STYLE}
          >
            <Popup>
              <ParkPopup park={park} />
            </Popup>
          </CircleMarker>
```

A `CircleMarker` is an SVG path. Leaflet's SVG renderer only gives it a CSS class, with no `tabindex`, no role and no keyboard handling (`node_modules/leaflet/src/layer/vector/SVG.js:93-108`). The `keyboard` option, which sets `tabIndex = '0'` and `role="button"`, only exists on `L.Marker` (`node_modules/leaflet/src/layer/marker/Marker.js:37-39` and `236-238`). So click and popup work with a mouse, but a keyboard user can never reach a marker. The `CircleMarker` was specified on purpose in `PLAN.md:165` (W2.T3) to avoid broken default icon images. Keyboard access wasn't considered.

**2. On desktop, the map comes before the list in the page.**

```63:73:src/pages/HomePage.tsx
      <ParkMap
        parks={parks}
        className="absolute inset-0 z-0 h-full w-full [&_.leaflet-left]:left-auto! [&_.leaflet-left]:right-0!"
      />
      <ParkListPanel
```

Tab order today:
1. The map itself, which Leaflet makes a tab stop (`Map.Keyboard.js:46-47`).
2. The zoom-in and zoom-out buttons.
3. The attribution link.
4. The search box and its clear button.
5. The list items.

Nothing follows the list. Wanting "list first, then map" means the list has to come first in the page.

**3. The map itself is a tab stop.** Even after reordering, the first stop on the map would be the map itself, not the first marker. Setting `tabindex="-1"` on it doesn't help: Leaflet overwrites any value of 0 or less with 0 (`Map.Keyboard.js:46`). Turning that off needs `keyboard={false}` on `MapContainer` (which loses arrow-key panning and +/- zoom) or resetting the attribute after the map is set up.

**4. Popups come after all markers.** Leaflet builds its layers first and its controls afterwards (`Map.js:1119-1122`), and the popup layer sits after the marker layer. Once markers are focusable, the order is: every marker, then any open popup's "View details" link, then the zoom buttons. If Enter opens a popup, Tab would go to the next marker, not into the popup.

**5. Marker order drifts from list order after a search.** Both start in the same order: `getParks()` sorts by name (`src/data/parks.ts:65-72`), `filterParks` keeps that order, and the list and `toMappable` loop over the same array. But react-leaflet adds markers in the order they mount. If you search "prospect" and then clear it, the Prospect marker stays first and every other marker is added after it. So markers can't rely on page order alone.

## (b) Proposed fix

1. **`ParkMap.tsx`: switch `CircleMarker` to `Marker` with a styled `L.divIcon`** (a small blue circle, keeping the current look).
   - Keep keyboard access on (the default) and give each marker a name (`title` plus an `aria-label`, for example "Prospect Park, show details").
   - Put the focus ring on the icon (`focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-primary focus-visible:ring-offset-2`, rounded), because the default Leaflet styles don't show one.
   - Parks with null coordinates are already skipped.
2. **Keep markers in list order.** Remount the markers whenever the visible set of parks changes, for example by keying a wrapper on the joined park ids. With about 12 parks this is cheap.
3. **Make Enter useful.** Leaflet already turns Enter on a focused marker into a click. Either:
   - on popup open, move focus to the "View details" link (and return it to the marker on Escape), or
   - make Enter go straight to `/park/:id`, skipping the popup.
4. **`HomePage.tsx` (desktop only): render the list panel before the map.** The layout is all absolute positioning plus `z-10`, so nothing moves on screen.
5. **Remove or keep the map's own tab stop** (see the second open decision).
6. **Side finding:** `TileLayer` has no OpenStreetMap credit (`ParkMap.tsx:64`), which `PLAN.md:165` asks for and the OSM licence requires. Worth adding in the same change.

## (c) Overhead

| Item | Estimate |
|---|---|
| Files changed | `src/components/map/ParkMap.tsx`, `src/pages/HomePage.tsx`, maybe a little CSS in `src/index.css` |
| Code | about 40–70 lines (about 35–55 in `ParkMap`, about 5 in `HomePage`) |
| Tests | new `src/components/map/ParkMap.test.tsx`, about 60–90 lines (details below) |
| Time | about 45–75 minutes including tests and manual keyboard checks |
| Risk | low to medium: matching the circle's look and ring offset with `divIcon`, focus moving into and out of the popup, and the remount-on-search approach |

The tests would check that marker icons have `tabindex="0"`, `role="button"` and names in list order, both before and after a search is cleared. They would also check that the list comes before the map on desktop and that Enter works. Leaflet runs in the test environment, but nothing is laid out, so these are checks on the page structure rather than on what appears on screen.

**Track boundaries:** the fix crosses tracks. `ParkMap.tsx` belongs to W2.T3, and `HomePage.tsx` belongs to W3.T1 and then W4.T1 (`PLAN.md:68-71`), all DONE. The only open track is W5.T1, which may edit any file but only for fixes. Under the bugfix pattern in your WTS rules, the clean route is a new bugfix track that owns both files. Folding it into W5.T1 also works if you treat it as a fix.

## (d) Decisions for you

1. **Mobile.** The list and map never appear together on mobile (`HomePage.tsx:93-108`), so "after the list" only means something on desktop. On the mobile map view, should "Show list" come first and then the markers? Today it comes after the map in the page.
2. **The map's own tab stop.** Keep it (arrow-key panning and +/- zoom, but one extra stop before the first marker), or remove it so Tab lands straight on the first marker?
3. **Zoom buttons and attribution.** After the markers (Leaflet's natural order), or before them?
4. **What Enter does on a marker.** Open the popup and move focus to "View details", or go straight to the detail page?
5. **"In view" versus all markers.** Today the map fits to show every park, so they're roughly the same. Leaflet pans to an off-screen marker when it gets focus (`Marker.js:82`). Should markers outside the current view be skipped, or all included?
6. **First list item without coordinates.** If it has no location, should "first marker" mean the first list item that does have one? I assumed yes.

I'm tracing the desktop tab order: the map container gets focus first with tabindex 0, then zoom controls, then the attribution link — and I'm noting that OSM attribution appears to be missing since the TileLayer lacks an attribution prop, which is a compliance issue worth flagging. After that the tab order moves into the panel with the search input, clear button, and list links.

Looking closer at marker ordering, parks are sorted by name and that order is preserved through filtering, but when a search filter is cleared, new markers get appended at the end rather than reinserted in sorted position since react-leaflet only adds/removes markers on mount/unmount — meaning a marker that stayed visible through a filter change ends up appearing before markers that get re-added, causing the DOM order to diverge from the visual list order. That's a real bug worth calling out rather than just a side note.

I'm weighing fixes: either remount the whole marker group with a key tied to the filtered query so markers always re-render in sorted order, or handle focus order manually via a keydown handler instead of relying on DOM order at all. I also need to check whether the first list item actually has coordinates, since the "first focused map item should match first list item" rule only makes sense for the first *mappable* item, not just the first item in the list — the Highland park case needs verifying.

For the desktop layout, the simplest fix is reordering the DOM so the list panel comes before the map panel, keeping the visual layout unchanged via positioning, but then I run into the leaflet container itself being tab-focusable (tabindex 0) and the Keyboard handler resetting any tabindex ≤ 0 back to 0, so setting it to -1 to skip past the container won't stick unless I disable the keyboard pan feature entirely.

I also want to use divIcon markers so focus-visible ring styles can be applied directly via Tailwind, since the div itself becomes the focusable element and should support box-shadow ring styling. Finally, I'm checking that pressing Enter on a focused marker triggers its click handler per Leaflet's built-in keypress behavior, opening the popup and making its contents (like a "View details" link) focusable in turn.

Leaflet's autoPanOnFocus means tabbing to an off-screen marker pans it into view, and since fitBounds shows everything initially, "in view" essentially covers all markers at start. For mobile, since map and list never coexist, I need to check the tab order on map view — the Show list button comes right after the map in the DOM.

The work touches both ParkMap.tsx and HomePage.tsx, crossing track boundaries since Waves 1-4 are already done; this fits as a fixes-only task or a new bugfix track. For testing, I'll verify Leaflet renders adequately in jsdom and write tests checking marker icons have proper tabindex, role, and aria-label ordering, that the list panel precedes the map in the DOM, and that Enter key activation works correctly.

I'm estimating roughly 100-150 lines of changes total with 45-75 minutes of work, and noting a side issue: the TileLayer is missing OSM attribution, which is a licensing requirement worth mentioning in the plan. The CircleMarker currently only opens its popup via mouse click, which I should address as well. Time to write it up.
